content_units: Movie Night Shortlist for Four Adults
Here are 8 strong picks that match   smart sci-fi or mystery  ,   low gore  ,   no sexual violence  ,   under 130 minutes  ,   1995–2020  , and   available in English  .
8 Films That Fit the Brief

Option 1:   Arrival (2016, 116 min)     A linguist is recruited to communicate with mysterious alien visitors whose language may change how humans understand time.     Why it fits:   intelligent sci-fi, emotionally rich, suspenseful without gore, and very discussion-friendly.     Best for:   thoughtful

Option 2:   Ex Machina (2014, 108 min)     A programmer is invited to test whether a humanoid AI has true consciousness inside a secluded tech estate.     Why it fits:   sleek, cerebral sci-fi mystery with tension and ethical questions, while staying mostly blood-light.     Best for:   tense

Option 3:   Coherence (2013, 89 min)     During a dinner party, a passing comet triggers bizarre reality shifts that make the guests doubt everything around them.     Why it fits:   sharp, twisty, low-budget-smart sci-fi with almost no gore and a great group-theory feel after the credits.     Best for:   tense

Option 4:   The Prestige (2006, 130 min)     Two rival magicians become locked in a dangerous obsession to outdo each other’s greatest illusion.     Why it fits:   brainy mystery thriller with excellent reveals, restrained on-screen violence, and broad crowd appeal.     Best for:   crowd-pleaser

Option 5:   Source Code (2011, 93 min)     A soldier repeatedly relives the last minutes before a train explosion to identify the bomber and stop a larger attack.     Why it fits:   fast-moving, clever sci-fi mystery with minimal gore and an easy hook for mixed tastes.     Best for:   crowd-pleaser

Option 6:   Moon (2009, 97 min)     Near the end of a lonely lunar work contract, an isolated astronaut discovers something deeply wrong with his mission.     Why it fits:   smart, intimate sci-fi with strong ideas, low violence, and a reflective mood.     Best for:   thoughtful

Option 7:   Searching (2018, 102 min)     A father investigates his missing daughter by piecing together her digital life through screens, messages, and search history.     Why it fits:   modern mystery with real momentum, very little gore, and an accessible format that keeps a group engaged.     Best for:   crowd-pleaser

Option 8:   Primer (2004, 77 min)     Two engineers accidentally create a device that bends time and quickly lose control of the consequences.     Why it fits:   ultra-smart sci-fi for viewers who enjoy puzzles, with negligible gore and a very short runtime.     Best for:   thoughtful
Best Picks by Mood
-   If you want the safest group pick:     Arrival   or   Source Code
-   If you want the most conversation after:     Coherence   or   Primer
-   If you want stylish tension:     Ex Machina
-   If you want a prestige thriller feel:     The Prestige
-   If you want something emotional and reflective:     Moon
-   If you want a modern mystery hook:     Searching
Viewing Notes for This Filter
Context note: “Little to no gore” was interpreted as   no horror-forward splatter and only limited brief violence  , and all picks were chosen to avoid   sexual violence  .
